record.original_question: Determine whether the vanishing micro-graphs that are indispensable for constructing and analyzing the dimension-(d+1) problem arise only by taking descendants of an underlying vanishing set already present in dimension d-1, rather than from genuinely new vanishing mechanisms appearing for the first time in higher dimension.

evidence.quote: Do these indispensable (cf. [6]) vanishing micro-graphs stem only from the underlying vanishing set in R d−1 through their descendants ?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setup. Consider Nambu–Poisson brackets on $\mathbb{R}^d$, defined for $f_1,\dots,f_d\in C^\infty(\mathbb{R}^d)$ by the Jacobian
$$\{f_1,\dots,f_d\}_{\mathrm{Nambu}} = \det\!\Big(\frac{\partial f_i}{\partial x^j}\Big)_{1\le i,j\le d}.$$
Within Kontsevich's graph calculus adapted to the Nambu setting, a "Nambu micro-graph" is a finite oriented graph whose internal vertices carry Casimir functions and whose edges encode partial derivatives, producing a multidifferential polynomial expression in the Casimirs and in a chosen multivector. A 1-vector Nambu micro-graph over $\mathbb{R}^d$ is called a vanishing micro-graph if the differential-polynomial expression it represents is identically zero on $\mathbb{R}^d$. Two known mechanisms for vanishing are:
(i) the existence of a graph automorphism $g$ with $g(\Gamma)\cong\Gamma$ acting by sign $-1$ on the associated expression, and
(ii) cancellation of disjoint pairs of terms after expansion, without such an automorphism.

Descendants. Given a Nambu micro-graph $\Gamma$ over $\mathbb{R}^{d-1}$, its $d$-dimensional descendants are the Nambu micro-graphs obtained by adjoining one new Casimir together with new edges to it and applying the Leibniz rule for each external arrow that lands on the enlarged Casimir factor; this produces a fixed linear combination of micro-graphs over $\mathbb{R}^d$.

Indispensable vanishing micro-graphs. A vanishing 1-vector Nambu micro-graph $\Gamma$ over $\mathbb{R}^d$ is called indispensable for dimension $d+1$ if it must be used (i.e. cannot be replaced or omitted) when constructing and verifying the solution of the tetrahedral flow / Kontsevich tetrahedral graph cocycle problem on Nambu–Poisson brackets in $\mathbb{R}^{d+1}$.

Question. Determine whether every indispensable vanishing 1-vector Nambu micro-graph over $\mathbb{R}^d$ arises as (a linear combination of) descendants of a vanishing Nambu micro-graph already present over $\mathbb{R}^{d-1}$, or whether genuinely new vanishing mechanisms — not reducible to descendants of any lower-dimensional vanishing micro-graph — first appear in dimension $d$ for some $d\ge 2$.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an open problem in a November 2025 preprint on Kontsevich graphs and Nambu–Poisson brackets, where the authors conjecture but do not establish whether all indispensable vanishing micro-graphs originate as descendants of lower-dimensional vanishing sets. No subsequent resolution was found.

status_evidence.title: arXiv:2511.06121 abstract
status_evidence.snippet: Investigates the open problem of (non)triviality for Kontsevich's tetrahedral graph cocycle action on Nambu–Poisson brackets; identifies a conjecturally infinite new set of differential-polynomial identities for d×d Jacobian determinants.
status_evidence.claim: The framework in which the question is posed is itself presented as an open problem; the descendants question is stated as an open question in the text.
